notes: Slide frames “Encapsulating the DbContext”: encapsulation protects data integrity and reduces a class API surface. The note says this applies to all code, not only domain model code.
Shows Program.cs/AddDbContext registering SchoolContext and configuring UseSqlServer, UseLoggerFactory and EnableSensitiveDataLogging directly in the application startup surface.
Shows CreateLoggerFactory filtering EF Core database command logs and writing to console, making logging configuration part of the DbContext setup details.
Console output screenshot highlights SQL command logging including parameter values; this motivates the warning that sensitive-data logging can expose query parameters.
Text rule: only use parameters that change depending on the environment.
Shows SchoolContext with private readonly fields _connectionString and _useConsoleLogger, DbSet properties, and a constructor accepting string connectionString and bool useConsoleLogger.

Shows OnConfiguring inside SchoolContext: UseSqlServer(_connectionString), then selects logging behavior based on _useConsoleLogger using CreateLoggerFactory or CreateEmptyLoggerFactory. This moves EF configuration detail from Program.cs into DbContext.
Shows a smaller AddScoped registration that constructs SchoolContext with builder.Configuration["ConnectionString"] and a boolean flag, instead of exposing the whole options-builder chain.
Recap slide: DbContext is encapsulated; the conventional AddDbContext options approach leaves too much room for data/configuration inconsistencies, similar to public setters.
Recap slide distinguishes simple configuration, which can stay as-is, from complex configuration, which is better to encapsulate.

Recap slide: the possible configuration options are reduced to a minimum. The client sees constructor parameters such as connectionString and useConsoleLogger, while EF configuration complexity is abstracted and encapsulated inside DbContext.
Recap slide: registering with AddScoped factory configures the DbContext as a scoped dependency; the two registration styles are equivalent in terms of DbContext lifetime.

Summary slide: encapsulated DbContext usage bundles dependencies and operations together, moves configuration logic to the DbContext, and encourages looking for encapsulation opportunities throughout code.
